title: US Payrolls Shock: June Jobs Rise Just 57K, Fed Hike Bets Pared Back
content: US non-farm payrolls rose by only 57,000 in June, well below the roughly 110,000-115,000 consensus, the BLS reported on 2 July. The unemployment rate fell to 4.2%, but chiefly because the participation rate slid to 61.5% — its lowest since March 2021 — whilst April and May payrolls were revised down by a combined 74,000. The miss led traders to scale back bets on a Fed rate hike as soon as September, with futures markets sharply paring probabilities. The USD index slipped towards 100.8, and gold extended its rally, breaking above $4,100/oz and touching near $4,170 by 3 July as reduced hike odds boosted the non-yielding metal. UST yields eased on the release.

title: Eurozone CPI Eases to 2.8%, Cooling ECB Hike Pressure; Stoxx 600 Hits Record
content: Eurozone headline CPI eased to 2.8% YoY in June from 3.2%, undershooting the 3.0% forecast, whilst core CPI slowed to 2.4% from 2.6%, data around 1 July showed. The softer print follows the ECB's 25bp hike on 11 June and has reduced pressure for a further move, with policymakers signalling no rush to tighten again; EUR slipped below $1.14 on the news. European equities capitalised on the shift, with the Stoxx 600 closing at a 52-week high of 652.77 on 3 July, up 0.69% on the day and notching a fourth consecutive weekly gain — its best week in over a month — led by defensive utilities and cyclicals.

title: Kospi Swings Wildly, Rebounds 5.8% as Samsung and SK Hynix Surge
content: South Korea's Kospi capped a volatile week, rebounding 5.76% on 3 July to reclaim the 8,000 level after tumbling towards 7,300 amid a renewed global AI-chip sell-off. Samsung Electronics jumped 8.2% and SK Hynix surged 10.9%, with sentiment lifted by reports that Samsung is pushing for up to 20% price hikes on Q3 DRAM contracts. The whipsaw echoed the prior week's AI-hardware demand jitters and rippled across Asian tech, whilst institutional investors were net buyers of over KRW4.46trn. Attention now turns to Samsung's preliminary Q2 earnings due 7 July and SK Hynix's Nasdaq ADR listing on 10 July, both seen as tests of the AI rally's durability.
